quest.title: Mary-Ann's Story
quest.description: You have arrived at "the real Annapausis."
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.num: Ann of the Narzissenkreuz: Act III
chapter.title: "If She No Longer Dreams of You..."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wants to say that the book's contents were really weird, but it's really not much when compared to this, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: The world should be like this, not like how it is outside. Children should be able to play under the sun and in the grass without fear of hindrance or harm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place does feel pretty comfy, yeah. Paimon feels way better than she did back when we were adventuring throughout the kingdom. There was no sunlight there at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Never mind that... This place really is nice! It's gotta be Princess Lyris's garden, right? Say, {NICKNAME}, when our adventures are over, why don't we find a place like this to live?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We can eat tasty fruits, plant lots of Sweet Flowers, and we can invite our friends over as guests! We could all live together happily. What do you say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, then it's agreed! Still, we should focus on helping Ann find the Princess first, huh?
Hide and seek, hide and seek, where did Mary and her friends go? ♪

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Sounds like someone's singing over there...

choices.text: ...Let's put a pin in that for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's true. We've gotta help Ann find the Princess first, don't we?

talks.objective: Find the owner of the voice

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!

talks.objective: Find the owner of the voice

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: My, what a pleasant surprise. It has been a long time since I've met someone from outside. Where are you from?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, well, we're...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, Paimon's not sure either. We defeated the fell dragon Narcissus, and then we ended up here somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: The "fell dragon Narcissus," you say? That must've been a frightening foe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Uh... Did you think so, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: My, I've heard that Narcissus has hurt many, and has turned many kingdoms to ash. Defeating him was an impressive feat indeed!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, so you know about him, too? Great! We're from the Narzissenkreuz Kingdom, and we're looking for Princess Lyris. Do you know where we might find her?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: "Princess Lyris," you say... I'm afraid I do not know.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But she should be here...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Is that the case, Ann? But I have lived here for a long, long time, and yet I have never seen any princess. Perhaps she might be somewhere else?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so? But before we came here, we read a book about that princess, and how she's beautiful and kind and stuff...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: #I'm afraid I'm unfamiliar with any such person... On the flipside, you, {NICKNAME}, do quite look like a {M#prince}{F#princess} from a distant land!
(You hear the sound of a bell...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Is that the bell?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Yes! That's the signal for teatime. In the past, the children would throw down their wooden swords the moment they heard this bell, and they would come into the hall to have snacks!

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: They're not here now, but I think it best to follow the rules all the same. They'd be quite disappointed otherwise, I suspect. Well then, shall we?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hurray, snacks!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You and Paimon enjoy the snacks together.\nThey look very beautiful, but they are tasteless like pure water.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: How were they?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, they were great... Although Paimon couldn't really... taste them? Are you on a low-sugar diet or something, Mary-Ann?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Hmm? My apologies, Paimon. I just made them as I remember them, so I'm not sure if they'll taste all that good...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, don't worry about it! At... at least Paimon's full now!

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Well, in that case, let me take you all out on a stroll!

choices.text: Thanks, but I'm not hungry at the moment...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe! In that case, your share's Paimon's!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon happily digs in.\nAs you watch her enjoy the snacks, you find yourself feeling a little peckish, too.

choices.text: In a manner of speaking, I suppose.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: This is a flower garden that we've painstakingly taken care of. Lovely, isn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I've heard Basil say that caring for children is like caring for a flower. You need good soil, sufficient sunlight, frequent watering, and you can't let them grow however they want.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe, sounds like this Basil is pretty smart!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: In fact, we must get rid of pests from time to time as well.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, actually, Basil sounds pretty dangerous too.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Ah, she is very capable indeed. Making snacks, caring for flowers, she can do it all. It would be nice if I could introduce her to you.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I have been caring for the flowers here all this time, in the hopes that some friends might come, and I might show them how they have bloomed. And well, here you are!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well... It's a shame that they aren't in bloom right now, though.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Well, we just need to water them, and they'll be fine!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Hide and seek, hide and seek, where did Mary and her friends go? ♪\nTo the halls of sea-born foam, to watch the sunflowers in bloom. ♪

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As the drops of water stain the soil of the garden black, the sunflowers spring from the earth, grow quickly, and bloom.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Aren't they beautiful?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? That was quick!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Well, they've been waiting for friends to arrive, after all. And with your arrival, ah, they were so excited! All they needed then was a little encouragement, a little rain to get them going.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, so that's how it is... Nature really is amazing, huh?

choices.text: I suspect this exceeds the realm of "amazing."

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Do you like them, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: They're very beautiful, like gleaming gold.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: I knew you would. I love them too, after all.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: #You're from a very, very faraway place, aren't you, {NICKNAME}? What sort of flowers bloom there?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: #{M#(Describe the flowers your sister wears in her hair.)}{F#The flowers I wear in my hair.}

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: #{M#Ah... Those do sound like lovely flowers.}{F#I thought those flowers were beautiful the moment I saw you.}

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But I fear that they'll be hard to find now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: ...Then let us speak of other flowers! I've always been in Fontaine, and I've never gone elsewhere. That said, a friend of mine has been to Sumeru. I heard from him that there are many flowers there that can't be found here.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Those that grow on cliffs, ones that only open at night. Some even grow on cacti...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Haha, and that's when he realized that there were no cacti in Fontaine, and had to give me a separate explanation. He was always the serious sort, and he was the smartest of us when we were young...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Ahem. Sorry, I'm talking to myself. It must be a little too exciting for me, meeting new friends like this. Well, then, Paimon. Have you seen any special flowers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Mondstadt's dandelions come to mind!

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Dandelions! Oh, do you have any of their delightful seeds with you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, well, we might?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Dandelions, dandelions, bloom, bloom, bloom~ ♪

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Dandelion seeds can indeed be found on Paimon.\nMary-Ann happily plants them in the soil.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Ah, yes! What sort of flower is a dandelion?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. Paimon thought you knew! Well, um, how should we put this... The dandelion flower is made of many tiny white flowers, and these white flowers have seeds on them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: When the wind blows, these tiny flowers will scatter along with the wind, and they will take root and sprout elsewhere, eventually making new flowers. Cool, huh?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Wow, they really are. I didn't know such a flower existed, but I have heard about something similar!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! What sorta flower is that?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: It's not a flower, but it's a story about water. In a certain place, there was a peaceful body of water...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Later, with disturbance, there came ripples, and droplets appeared in those ripples, droplets that had life in them. This life left the water, and turned into different forms.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: But though they were all made of water, gulfs opened between them due to these differences. Each drop of life was very weak, but each was beautiful in its own way.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: The dandelions you spoke of, Paimon, reminded me a lot of that story. A flower that was once united as one would be separated, would bloom, and each piece would become itself.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: But a single drop of water is weak and will dry up easily. Together, they will be strong... and yet, they will no longer be themselves. Is that how it is with dandelions, too?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Do you think that's a good thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Um... Paimon doesn't really get it. What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: They may be weak, but the distance is necessary.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: #...I think I understand where you're coming from, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What you're talking about sounds like what happened to Al, Petit Chou, and the others. To help us, they melded into one, turning into that big bubble...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Yes. I still remember.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Well. It might be meaningless to say this now.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Let's have a little walk again, shall we? Ah, yes! I can take you to see our dog!

choices.text: It might not be a bad thing for them to unite.
People can unite and yet maintain their personhood.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Hmm. Can they, really?

dialogues.speaker: "Doggie"
dialogues.text: #{M#Noble Sir}{F#Noble Miss}, it is an honor to receive food from you. A pleasure to see you again as well, Ms. Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Oh, you good doggie!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... good doggie?

dialogues.speaker: "Doggie"
dialogues.text: And how do you do, dear little Miss?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, uh, thanks for being polite and all, but... Ann, what's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I don't know... But this can't be Mori.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: He has always kept me company.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm. Does this mean that we've been wrong all along about what dogs really look like?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Water can take any shape, and life can choose what form it must take. This, however, has nothing to do with its essence. That is a different matter.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, didn't Al say something similarly weird?

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: I have heard something similar said, that the body is a prison that restricts evolution. That person was once a child, like all the others.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: We and many others heard him tell many stories. About how all life was originally formless, like water, and how there were no barriers between souls, thus allowing them to compose an endless story.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Many have forsaken their bodies, for if water can be withdrawn from blood, so too, can will be drawn out from one's form.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: ...But if you were to try to sprinkle water on the blackened dust that remains, it will not become blood again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I... I remember something... Even though I really didn't want to.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: How much do you remember, Ann?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: ...I don't know. There's just this flood of... feelings and scenes. Happy words and angry ones... I'm not sure...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: I understand.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: You go first, alright? And remember, be a good dog.

response.speaker: "Doggie"
response.text: Understood. See you, Ms. Mary-Ann. See you, dear guests.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, this is bad. The number of things that don't make sense just keeps going up! If we hadn't seen the dog, Paimon would've forgotten all that stuff already!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't we say we were going to rescue Princess Lyris?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: That's right...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: My apologies, but there is no Princess here. Only us. Today, we were simply fortunate to receive guests.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: But this is the end of the path. She has to be here!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But Mary-Ann said...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, so, that's gotta mean that one of you is mistaken, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Right? {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course! You've got the bigger brain here, don't you?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Paimon, all we experienced so far was just a "story."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, b—but didn't we team up with the Narzissenkreuz Adventure Team to defeat Narcissus's henchmen? Wasn't that real?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Think about it for a moment, Paimon...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is there even a Narzissenkreuz Kingdom amongst the seven nations?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh. You're right. Paimon didn't think of that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, the adventure team... Al, Petit Chou, Colonel Kate, Jak, Mori, the two of us... and our adventures... They were all just characters in a story?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, that can't be! Paimon can't accept that!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Didn't we encounter all kinds of stuff after going through the portal in the tower? There's a lot of stuff there that wouldn't fit if this was just a story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Y'know, like how there was no Holy Blade mentioned at the start, and how a sealed tower still had monsters and Bubble Formations inside it!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #Paimon... I think I understand what {NICKNAME} is trying to say. So, all the things that happened after we ascended the tower are things outside the realm of the story. Is that right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: More accurately, those parts of the story have not yet been written.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: So, the Holy Blade, Narcissus... These were still inside the story. It's just that they had not been arranged correctly yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon still finds it hard to imagine anyone who would create such a huge building just for a story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I believe the structure already existed.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It was just used as the setting for the story.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: So that means that the things I recalled along the way were things that happened here before... and I'm just a character in a story...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You're not merely a character.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: The fact that you can think about this means that you can remember it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if that's the case, who is Ann...?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: I am... Ann. I must rescue Princess Lyris...

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: #Alright, {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and dearest Ann. Our time is up. I enjoyed our time together, but I'm afraid it is time for you to leave.

response.speaker: Mary-Ann
response.text: Why did you have to say it was fiction if you already knew? Spare a thought for Ann's feelings, at least...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm?

choices.text: Do you really want to hear what I have to say?
Don't fuss over the details too much.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? What happened!?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: B—But...!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Shh. There's no need to say anything, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I once heard my best friend tell a story about a beautiful princess trapped in a high tower.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Before you arrived, I had a dream. I dreamed that I was a small, brave Oceanid, and we set out to save the Princess...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: And perhaps there are princesses in this world, and dragons, too. But I also know that the world's affairs are rarely this simple. Why would a dragon be concerned with a princess, after all?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: After waking up, I would find this dream laughable, yet nostalgic, every time I thought about it. Do you remember now, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No! There has to be some other way. If I can't save Princess Lyris... Then what of my birth? My only wish? Do they have no meaning?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Don't say that, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Your birth was a beautiful accident. As things stand, "I" can only wish for you to live on for your own sake. Go, see the world, and see how it has changed these past years.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I wish for you to have your own soul, memories, personality, and wishes.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I wish for you to be the master of your own fate, and to experience all the beauty of the real world. Can you do that for me?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: #It was a pleasure to meet you, {NICKNAME}, Paimon — and it was my pleasure to meet you too, Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: But the Annapausis is our tomb. I do not wish for you to linger here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann... Why are you saying that? We can find a way to help you, can't we?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: #Haha. I sense that you are good-hearted and powerful indeed. Thank you, Paimon, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: I'm just someone who sometimes enjoys dreaming of lovely adventures and wonderful futures. But I know what happened in the past. I already know that there's no going back.

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: In the real world, everything has already ended... so this is farewell.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, y'know, Paimon just realized that this name has something to do with the Kingdom and Adventure Team in Ann's story...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: C'mon, we were busy adventuring — there wasn't that much time for Paimon to think!

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Do you know of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yup, and we also met some people who are really connected to it. They might be able to help us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: In any case, let's go!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true. Narzissenkreuz Kingdom... Adventure Team... Yeah, they seem connected, alright.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Do you have any idea where this Ordo might be?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: No...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, that's right. We're very experienced adventurers — if you need it found, we'll find it!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mary-Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, y'know, Paimon's sure we've heard this name before...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Feels like that book we saw in the Institute of Natural Philosophy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh. Paimon doesn't know. But it feels different somehow...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Huh. Just like in the book Canotila found.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah. That's... really odd...
Hide and seek, hide and seek, where did Mary and her friends go? ♪\nTo a great sea without borders, to the place from which all lives flow. ♪

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey there!
Oh, hi!
I'm sorry. I was just preparing some tea and didn't notice you. Come, sit. Snacks will be ready soon!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, snacks!
Yes, and ours are very good.
Ah, but I must say this first. We can only start once the bell rings. It would be quite rude to do otherwise.
#Where are you from, by the way? Why, you are a fascinating combination, aren't you? {M#A handsome young man}{F#A lovely young lady}, a small little Oceanid, and your beautiful, floating friend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hehe. Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Huh. Is it just Paimon, or does Ann look unhappy?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (She might have been reminded of something.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, and this Oceanid is our friend, Ann!

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Oh, my. A fine name indeed. In that case, please call me Mary-Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ann...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: #I'm sorry, Knight {NICKNAME}, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I had already started to feel that some things were off earlier in the adventure. As you led me off the story's track, I started to understand and recall some things.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: But I... still want to rescue "Princess Lyris." That is the reason for which I was born. I want to save her and bring this story to a happy end.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I mean, I don't even know who she is. I only know that she is a gentle, lovely princess, trapped due to Narcissus's invasion.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Ann, at least... at least we had fun while traveling with the adventure team, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Um, {NICKNAME}... Did you know that things would turn out this way?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No. I thought we could help Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if that's the case, we can still help Ann.

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't understand anything Mary-Ann said there at the end. Did you, Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Ann
dialogues.text: I did, sort of. I could sense that she was speaking of something terrible that happened in the past...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, Paimon feels that that's unfair — not just to you, Ann, but to us too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's why we've gotta find out what happened, at least. If we do, we can come up with some sort of plan!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Whether it be saving the Princess or figuring out what Mary-Ann said, or whatever, we just wanna help you, Ann! Isn't that right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Okay...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Still, if this is all just a story, then there's one thing Paimon doesn't get. What role do we play, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I can't be sure, but I think we're most likely...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: And that's why we can bring this story to an end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, Paimon gets it. So that's why Ann found us and brought us into the story.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #You might not have thought about it, Ann, but since we've been able to knock this story off course, that means that we've opened all sorts of unknown possibilities. Isn't that right, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You could say that.

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: #*sniff* Thank you, Knight {NICKNAME}. Thank you, Paimon...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's why we also need your help, Ann. And since we need to continue our adventure, well... Can you think of anything that could help us figure out what to do next?

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: Hmm... Let me think...

response.speaker: Ann
response.text: My memories contain a place known as the <color=#00E1FFFF>Narzissenkreuz Ordo</color>. This place appears to have very deep connections to past events.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, so you've got a dog, Mary-Ann?

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: Yes. He's a silly dog who has always accompanied me, and that's also why he's my best friend.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, Paimon doesn't see him, though...

dialogues.speaker: Mary-Ann
dialogues.text: #He'll come when it's feeding time. Since you're my guest, {NICKNAME}, please, do the honors.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Your vision blurs and you suddenly feel weightless, as the temperature of the once-warm air plunges rapidly.\nIt is as if you have slipped and fallen into frozen waters.
